summary: Elk County, PA steel Aermotor fire tower built 1926 for the state forestry department; removed around 1990 and found gone, with woods on the site, in 2004.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower; 80-ft steel fire tower topped by a 7 x 7 x 9 ft steel cab with 4-ft glass windows on all sides
facts.status_note: Abandoned and removed; a 2004 station recovery found the location a dense wooded area
facts.agency: Allegheny National Forest per Forest Lookouts; the 1926 USGS description names the Pennsylvania State Department of Forests and Waters

events.note: Steel Aermotor tower built 1926 per FFLOS; the NGS text quoted on Forest Lookouts says the USGS described it in 1926
FFLOS says removed circa 1990, so the year is approximate
Station recovery note (2004) found the tower abandoned and removed and the location wooded

notes_for_editor: Two sources, both read. The NGS survey text is only seen as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not on the NGS site. The agency value (Allegheny National Forest) comes from Forest Lookouts only and is not confirmed elsewhere; the 1926 description names the state department instead. Removal date is approximate (circa 1990). No staffing or fire record was found in the sources read, so the story omits staffing. A WebSearch found a 2007 Bradford Era column listing seven Elk State Forest towers built 1920-1925 without Hanley; it does not settle the date and is not cited.
